observations: A large purple-red rounded form dominates the center, containing three distinct toothed-mouth shapes and spiral-coiled eye marks at different scales.
White outline lines run loosely over the whole surface, while yellow and orange loops accent the eye areas against the underlying purple and blue cross-hatched fill.
The olive-green background is covered edge-to-edge with small rectangular scribble units in yellow, orange, and teal, creating a dense grid-like surround.
reading: Three toothed openings are stacked and nested inside one bulging form, each paired with coiled eye marks, so the image reads as faces within a face. The white outline sits above dense purple and blue cross-hatching rather than containing it, giving the surface a layered, pressured feeling. The surrounding grid of small scribbled rectangles holds the central form in without framing it calmly.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #9 and nnxyz nnotb #11 show how differently the same line vocabulary can land: #9 spreads figures across open space, #11 dissolves into an all-over field, while #10 compresses both impulses into one dense stacked form.

connections.reason: Both works layer loose white outlines over a dense multi-color scribbled fill, using that white line to define large shapes against a busy ground — the collector's noted visual link between nnxyz and scrimshaw.
nnxyz nnotb #11 replaces all figural structure with a pure cross-hatched field, making it a direct contrast to #10's use of the same cross-hatch as interior fill beneath recognizable stacked forms.

lookingQuestion: How many separate toothed openings can you locate, and does the layering suggest some sit behind others or do they all appear on the same surface?
ambiguities: Title-derived order and recorded-creation order align for this work in the owned subset, but gaps elsewhere in the nnotb family mean neither confirms an unbroken sequence.
The scrimshaw GM connection rests on the collector's stated visual perspective; no shared subject or confirmed formal influence can be established from the images alone.
